0.meaning: A method for evaluating individuals where multiple assessors observe a single person across different exercises and score them independently.

1.meaning: A complete assessment center cycle for a specific group of individuals; container for candidates and exercises.

2.meaning: The individual being assessed in this project. Each candidate has a "journey" with sequential statuses.

3.meaning: An assessment activity such as an interview, group discussion, presentation, or in-basket.

4.meaning: The observable capability being assessed (e.g., "Decision Making" or "Teamwork"). Each exercise assesses multiple competencies.

5.meaning: A person who observes the candidate during an exercise and scores them independently of other assessors.

6.meaning: The link between "this assessor × this candidate × this exercise". The only thing that grants the assessor permission to record evidence and scores.

7.meaning: An objective behavioral note recorded by the assessor during the exercise; serves as the basis for the score.

8.meaning: Text accepted by the candidate before starting. Defined at the organization level, not the project; only one version is active at any time.

9.meaning: An advisory report on how many methods assess each competency and whether any assessor's workload exceeds the target. It is a warning, not a blocker.

10.meaning: A meeting where assessors gather after exercises conclude to reach an agreed (consensus) score for each candidate × competency.

11.meaning: The final score determined during the wash-up meeting through group consensus, replacing the raw scores of individual assessors.

12.meaning: When the range of raw scores from different assessors for a candidate × competency is wide (discrepancy) — an indication that further discussion is needed before recording the consensus score.

adminConsole.intro: This page is the assessment center control room. First, open a project using the selector at the top, then work on that project within the "Overview", "Candidates", "Exercises", and "Assignments" tabs. The "Settings" tab is at the organization level and is not tied to a project. The entire setup has six steps, and the "Overview" checklist always shows which step has been completed and which one is next.

youCan.5: Advance each candidate's journey status by one step.
youCan.7: In the "Reports & Publication" tab, view the R2 report and publish or cancel after consensus.
youCan.8: In the "Analytics" tab, view the aggregate report, inter-rater reliability (ICC), assessor calibration, and candidate rankings.
youCan.9: Undo mistakes: edit project and exercise details, disable redundant exercises, and revoke incorrect invitations before consent is recorded.

managerReport.intro: Unlike the published report, this page is never shown to the candidate. Here you can see the consensus score for each competency along with the session discussion notes, recorded narrative, and statistical discrepancy badge (comparing the consensus score with the mechanical mean/median of raw scores) — for reviewing the quality of the consensus process itself, not for public display.
managerReport.title: Internal Manager Report Guide (R2)

youCan.0: View the consensus score for each competency and the wash-up session discussion notes.
youCan.1: Review the result narrative recorded for the candidate.
youCan.2: Check the discrepancy badge and the mechanical mean/median of each competency for quality review.

The content of the report is frozen by the assessment center manager at the moment of publication; any badge next to a competency indicates how many observations this level was derived from and whether it is based on the final key/definition or a draft.

youCan.0: View your published report for any project/cycle in which you were a candidate.
youCan.1: Read the transparency badge for each competency to understand where the result came from.
youCan.2: Print the report or save it to PDF.

youCan.1: Write and save the level and justification for each competency.

activate.lockedBecause: You must first create a project or select one from the picker above.
activate.title: 6) Activate the project
activate.why: Activation means setup is complete and execution begins. As long as it is a draft, everything remains in preparation mode.

assignments.lockedBecause: You must first have at least one candidate and one exercise in this project.
assignments.title: 5) Assign assessors to candidate × exercise
assignments.what: For each exercise, specify which assessor observes which candidate.
assignments.why: Assessors only see their own assignments; without assignments, the assessor console will be empty and scoring will not be possible.

candidates.lockedBecause: You must first create a project or select one from the picker above.
candidates.title: 3) Invite candidates
candidates.what: Select the individuals to be assessed by searching for their names.
candidates.why: Each candidate starts with the "Invited" status and their "My Assessment Journey" page becomes active.

consent.title: 1) Enable the consent form text
consent.what: Write a consent form text and "activate" it.
consent.why: Until there is an active text, no candidate can give consent, and the entire journey stops at the very first step. Creating the text is not enough — activation is a separate and deliberate action.

exercises.lockedBecause: You must first create a project or select one from the picker above.
exercises.title: 4) Define exercises and their competencies
exercises.what: Exercise = an assessment activity (interview, group discussion, presentation...). Specify which competencies each exercise measures.
exercises.why: Scoring is only possible on the competencies of that specific exercise; an exercise without competencies will appear empty for the assessor.

project.title: 2) Create an assessment project
project.what: Project = an assessment center cycle for a group of people (e.g., "Middle Managers Assessment Center — Fall").
project.why: Candidates, exercises, and assignments all sit under a project; without a project, there is nowhere to add them.

canceled.label: Canceled
canceled.meaning: The session has been canceled and can no longer be opened.

draft.label: Draft
draft.meaning: The session has been created but not yet opened; only the agenda (candidates/participants) can be edited.

locked.label: Locked
locked.meaning: Both confirmations have been submitted; the summary is final and cannot be changed except via a post-lock amendment request.

open.label: Open
open.meaning: The session is in progress; consensus scores for pending candidates can be entered and edited.

agenda.title: 1) Create the agenda
agenda.what: Add wash-up-ready candidates and participants (at least two people).
agenda.why: Without at least one candidate and two participants, there is no session to open.

consensus.lockedBecause: You must open the session first.
consensus.title: 3) Record the consensus score for each cell
consensus.what: For each candidate × competency, record a level and a note after discussion.
consensus.why: The algorithmic suggestion is only a reference — the decision belongs to the group; empty cells block final locking.

lock.lockedBecause: All agenda cell consensus scores must be recorded first — no empty cells may remain.
lock.title: 4) Final Lock — Two separate confirmations
lock.what: Two different people must record "First Confirmation" and "Second Confirmation" by explicitly typing the word "lock".
lock.why: Locking means the summary is definitive; afterwards, any change is only possible through a "revision request" and the second person's approval.

openSession.lockedBecause: First, the agenda must have at least one waiting candidate and two participants.
openSession.title: 2) Open the session
openSession.what: Move the session from "Draft" to "Open" — this action is reversible.
openSession.why: Recording the consensus score and viewing raw assessor scores is only possible during an open session.
